newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel defends Coke Amatil deal.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel defends Coke Amatil deal.

text.p: Food and beverages firm San Miguel Corp on Tuesday strongly defended its deal with Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil at its annual meeting attended by over 2,000 shareholders.

"This is a magnificient opportunity for CCBPI and its people. There are substantial long-term benefits for CCBPI and for the shareholders of San Miguel, and any negatives in the short-term, if any, will be minimal," San Miguel Chairman Andres Soriano III told stockholders.
Early this month, San Miguel said it was merging its 70 percent owned subsidiary Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc (CCBPI) in exchange for a 25 percent stake in Coca-Cola Amatil.
San Miguel shares have come under pressure since the merger was announced on April 3, with some analysts saying the Philippine company was getting the worse end of the deal.
It involves a share swap through which CCBPI will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Coca-Cola Amatil, and San Miguel will own 25 percent of Amatil's stock.
Following the swap, San Miguel would become Coca-Cola Amatil's second largest shareholder after the Coca-Cola Co, Soriano said.
Coca-Cola Amatil is Coca-Cola's largest bottler outside the U.S., he said.
The swap had been approved by San Miguel's board of directors and was awaiting clerance from the concerned regulatory bodies and shareholders.
Analysts who criticised the deal said CCBPI was one of San Miguel's most profitable divisions and the company would have to reckon with the loss of its large cash flows.
San Miguel's traditional strength is in beer, a market it still dominates in the Philippines, but its growth has been stunted in recent years as steep taxes have forced the company to raise prices.
"This company needs, and is ready, to grow and diversify from a single market and evolve with the changing dynamics of the worldwide soft drinks industry," Soriano said.

Soriano, in his defence of the deal, said the alliance would combine the operating and technical skills of Coca-Cola Amatil and CCBPI "into a powerhouse team with enhanced economies of scale in the purchase of raw materials, broader access to capital markets and the capability of expanding franchise territory".
